behavior: A disabled `<fieldset>` disables each form part in it as its `disabled` prop does: `RadioGroup`, `Radio`, `CheckboxGroup`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `NumberField`, `Select`, `Slider`, `OTPField`, `Combobox`, `Autocomplete`, `DateField`, `TimeField`, `DatePicker`, `DateRangePicker` and `TimePicker` with their popups, `Field.Root` and its parts, `Field.Item`, `Input` and `Fieldset.Root`. A native `<fieldset disabled>` counts as HTML disables a form control, except in its first `<legend>`, and `Fieldset.Root` with `disabled` counts also with no `Field.Root`. The parts then have `data-disabled` or the native `disabled`, and `aria-disabled` where the part sets it. A press, Space or a stepper button changes no value, Tab skips such a radio, checkbox or switch, the arrow keys skip such a radio, a radio group in such a fieldset has no tab stop, and `Form` leaves out the value of each such field. A native fieldset takes effect after the mount, and the parts follow each later change of it. Base UI follows only `Fieldset.Root` through `Field.Root`. In a native disabled fieldset, its parts show no disabled state, Tab focuses a radio, a checkbox or a switch, and a press or Space changes its value: the root dispatches a click to the disabled input, and the browser runs the listeners of a click that a script dispatches. A press on a Number Field stepper changes the value, because the press starts on `pointerdown`, and `Form` gives the value of each such field to `onFormSubmit`. These native button parts also follow a disabled fieldset: `Button`, `Toggle`, `Tabs.Tab`, and the triggers of Accordion and Collapsible. The native button triggers of Dialog, Alert Dialog, Drawer, Menu, Popover, Date Picker, Date Range Picker, Time Picker, Navigation Menu and Tooltip follow it too. Each has `data-disabled` and the `disabled` slot state. A disabled trigger cannot open its popup on hover, and a fieldset that becomes disabled cancels a hover open that waits. Tabs keeps its selected panel, because only the `disabled` prop of a tab changes the selection. A fieldset does not disable a part whose `nativeButton` prop is `false`. `Tooltip.Trigger` checks its element, because it has no `nativeButton` prop. Its `disabled` prop still suppresses only the tooltip, with `data-trigger-disabled`. Base UI gives these native buttons no fieldset state, and its hover triggers can open their popups in a disabled fieldset.
